31.apl.582.2023.Judgment.odt

4.  After service of the notice, none appears for the non-applicant No.2.
5.

Present application is preferred by the applicant, who is the husband for quashing of the FIR in connection with Crime No.89/2015 registered with Police Station Shirkhed, District Amravati for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
6. The crime is registered on the basis of a report lodged by the non-applicant No.2 on an allegation that her marriage was performed with the present applicant on 25.05.2009.
After marriage, she resumed cohabitation at the house of the present applicant.
She is having one son from the said wedlock.

She cohabited with the present applicant for one year, thereafter she came to know that the present applicant is having some relations with one lady and on that count, the applicant started harassing her and also demanded the amount of Rs.1,00,000/- from her parents and subsequently she was constrained to leave the matrimonial house.
On the basis of the said report, police have registered the crime against the present applicant.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant appeared though video conferencing and submitted that even accepting the allegation as it is at its face value, no prima facie case is made out against the present applicant as the entire allegations 31.apl.582.2023.Judgment.odt levelled against the present applicant are omnibus, vague and general in nature.
No specific instances are narrated as far as the applicant is concerned.
He submitted that as the matrimonial dispute arose between the husband and wife, this FIR came to be lodged.

He also invited my attention towards the withdrawal pursis filed by the non-applicant No.2,
which shows that she has already settled the dispute with the present applicant and the withdrawal pursis is already filed before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No.2, Morshi.

sentences.text: The said compromise is already recorded by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class in the Domestic Violence (DV) proceedings also.

Thus, he submitted that now the non-applicant No.2 has already received the Mehr amount and she is not interested to proceed with the proceedings and therefore,
on that ground also the application deserves to be allowed.
8.
Per contra, learned APP submitted that there is specific allegations against the present applicant as far as the ill-treatment at his hands is concerned.
In view of that, the application deserves to be rejected.

9. On perusal of the recitals of the FIR, admittedly, the non-applicant No.2 has not given any specific instances as far as the demand of money and the ill-treatment at the hands of the present applicant is concerned.
It is apparent that general and vague allegations are levelled against all the family members in the said FIR and thereafter various proceedings are filed by the non-applicant No.2.
It is further apparent from the record that during the various matrimonial proceedings, the parties arrived at a settlement and compromise pursis is already filed before the trial Court.
The said settlement is already recorded before the trial Court.

10. Despite the service of notice, non-applicant No.2 has not appeared before this Court and has not put forth her contention whether she is opposing for quashing of FIR or stickup with the compromise.
11. Even accepting the allegation as it is, it has to be seen whether the offence under Section 498-A of IPC is made or not.
Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code prescribes punishment where a woman is subjected to cruelty by her husband or his relatives.
The offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also provides for fine.
The explanation appended to the provision defines "cruelty" in two 31.apl.582.2023.Judgment.odt parts.

Clause (a) refers to wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to her life, limb or health, whether mental or physical.

Clause (b) expands the scope of the term to include harassment with a view to coercing the woman or her relatives to meet any unlawful demand for property or valuable security, or on account of failure to meet such demand.
12. In view of the above legal requirement, if the allegations made by the victim are taken into consideration admittedly vague, general and omnibus allegations are levelled against the applicant.
It is also apparent that merely because there is a dispute arose between husband and wife the FIR came to be lodged.
No specific instances are narrated as far as the physical or mental ill-treatment is concerned.

Now it is well settled that in absence of the specific averments as to the ill-treatment, the allegations which are not substantiated by any material, the Court has to exercise the inherent powers in favour of the parties.
In view of that, the application deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass following order:
ORDER (i) The application is allowed.

(ii) The FIR in connection with Crime No.89/2015 registered with Police Station Shirkhed, District Amravati for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
